newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures plunge by daily limits.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures plunge by daily limits.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo corn futures plunged by their 500-yen daily limits except for the limitless spot November contract at the close on Friday, following the lower Chicago market overnight, traders said.
Limitless November contract was down 820 yen per tonne at 15,280 yen. Benchmark September dropped by the 500-yen daily limit to 15,190 yen. Daily volume was 64,491 lots.
Most contracts fell by their limit in early afternoon, as long-liquidation overwhelmed bargain-hunting buying.
"Long-liquidation were stimulated by the view that the Chicago market will slip further," one trader said.
Expectations that the corn crop in the United States will be good this year stimulated long-liquidation.
"Market sentiment remains bearish. But support at 15,000 yen for the benchmark September should be maintained because of caution over oversold conditions," the trader said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.91-1/2 per bushel at 0820 GMT, down by 0-1/2 U.S. cents from Thursday's close.
The spot November of the CBOT soybean futures was at $7.38-1/2 at 0820 GMT, up by 1.00 cent from Thursday.
